items.headline: World markets rebound as AI stocks recover on Wall Street
items.summary: Global markets advanced after a recovery in AI-related stocks on Wall Street. Nvidia had fallen sharply in premarket trading before the broader rebound.

items.headline: Nvidia shares fall as board launches probe involving Jensen Huang
items.summary: Nvidia shares were reported down about 4.4% in premarket trading as the company’s board launched a probe involving CEO Jensen Huang, adding governance risk to a major AI bellwether.

items.headline: Nvidia CEO crisis tests investor confidence in AI leadership
items.summary: The report frames the controversy around Jensen Huang as a test for the leader of a company central to the AI investment trade.

items.headline: Tech remains central to the U.S. stock-market outlook despite AI selloff
items.summary: Reuters reported that technology shares remain critical to the market’s direction because of their large weight in the S&P 500. The article also noted upcoming Nvidia earnings on November 17 and Dell earnings on November 24.

items.headline: Daily market report flags Microchip guidance below consensus
items.summary: A market report said Microchip Technology fell 10% after providing fiscal third-quarter non-GAAP earnings and revenue guidance that was below consensus estimates.

items.headline: AI trade recovery follows sharp technology selloff
items.summary: Market commentary described a rebound in AI-related shares after a major technology selloff, while investors continued reassessing valuations and data-center spending risks.

items.headline: Weekly market update highlights AI concentration and diversification risk
items.summary: ATB Financial reported a broad technology-led selloff and emphasized portfolio diversification as investors reassessed exposure to artificial intelligence themes.

items.headline: Market commentary says AI repricing has spread beyond chip stocks
items.summary: The report said the AI repricing had extended beyond listed semiconductor companies into AI infrastructure credit, private-market valuations and capacity contracts.
